key_insight: Stitching artifacts from patch-based generation can silently degrade output quality and downstream segmentation, even when perceptual scores look acceptable.
clinical_relevance: For biomedical image generation, especially large-volume datasets, careful stitching strategy matters because artifacts may affect the reliability of AI-assisted image analysis.
method: Compared three patch stitching approaches in cycleGAN-based style transfer.
Compared 2D versus 3D patch dimensionality on cryo-electron microscopy volumes.
Evaluated both perceptual quality and mitochondria segmentation performance, including orthogonal ensembling.
evidence_signal: FID failed to detect subtle stitching artifacts, while downstream segmentation revealed meaningful differences; 3D artifact-free stitching performed slightly better than 2D, and 2D trained more stably.
watch_item: Perceptual metrics alone are insufficient, so implementation should include task-based evaluation to catch artifacts that may not be visually obvious.
paper_title: Stitching and dimensionality effects on large artificially generated volume datasets
